current.title: California Lost 96% Of Its Kelp Forests. Blame One Missing Predator.
current.hook: A mystery disease wiped out billions of sea stars in 2013.
current.closing: No sea stars, no kelp, no forest. One disease did all that.
current.question: Did you know one disease could take down a whole forest? Tell me below.

segments.topic: sea stars wiped out by disease
segments.say: In 2013, a mystery wasting disease killed billions of sunflower sea stars almost overnight -- up to 99% of them, gone within two years.

segments.topic: urchins take over without their main predator
segments.say: Sea stars used to keep purple urchins in check. Without them, urchin numbers exploded -- up more than 10,000% along the North Coast.
Those urchins mowed down the kelp forest the whole ecosystem depends on. California's north coast lost 96% of its kelp canopy in just a few years.

held_for: judge: Recycled bubble charts and a text-only urchin 'race' with a perched mascot. No sea star, urchin or kelp ever appears, so the ecological chain reaction is never shown.

judge.one_line: Recycled bubble charts and a text-only urchin 'race' with a perched mascot. No sea star, urchin or kelp ever appears, so the ecological chain reaction is never shown.
problems: The hook is a slowly growing chart bubble with the mascot standing on it, not an event that gives a reason to stay (hook@0.3, hook@2.2).
seg0 and seg3 use the same bubble-compare machine, so two of the three data beats look alike.
seg2 shows the 10,000% urchin explosion as the text '10.1K%', and the mascot covers the 'Before 2014' label.
The mascot perches or cheers in place in every scene. He never acts out predation, grazing or collapse.
The closing scale uses land-tree icons to stand for kelp canopy, and the story's actual chain (stars → urchins → kelp) is never pictured.
The source line is truncated with '...' in the hook and seg0.
fixes: Open on the event itself: a field of sea stars dissolving to 1 in 100 in the first second.
Show urchins as a multiplying purple carpet for seg2 and write '10,000%' in full. Keep labels clear of the mascot.
Show seg3 as a kelp canopy seen from above (or a kelp forest) shrinking to 4% of its area as urchins graze it, not a repeat of the bubble machine.
Give Data one bit per beat tied to the stat, e.g. counting the few sea stars left, getting swamped by urchins, or holding up the last kelp frond.
Swap the closing scale's land trees for kelp, or recap the chain as a toppling sequence: star → urchin → kelp.

rules: TITLE or HOOK must contain a consequential NUMBER from the data below (the gate refuses a title+hook with no digit in either).

TITLE must be a PREMISE, not a searchable noun phrase: more than five words, or a number, or a question mark, or a tension word. 'Oldest Written Languages' is the failure; 'Why 3 of the 5 Oldest Scripts Are Still Unreadable' is the shape.

Every segment's TOPIC (a 2-4 word on-screen label) must share at least one real word with the TITLE — the gate checks a keyword bridge from each segment to the headline. Rename the topic, or write the title so it names what the segments are about.

Every NUMBER you say in a segment's SAY must be one that segment's data can show: a listed value, a difference between two of them, a percent change, a share of the total, or the same value in a bigger unit. A number from nowhere is refused — a guard derives every spoken quantity from the listed points.
Keep every number that is already correct. Do not add a country, company or person the data does not name.
Each SAY is one spoken sentence or two, at most 40 words, and says its beat's headline number out loud.
TOPIC labels are printed on the video: at most 4 words, no clause.

The HOOK is a 2000s download-site ad, not a fact read aloud: 6-14 words, the VIEWER is the one it happens to ('your coffee', 'your town'), lead with the shock, a visceral verb (wiped out, vanished, doubled, gone), one number from the data. Never a quiz ('Which animal...', 'Did you know...'), never a hedge (might, may, perhaps). Exaggerate the FEELING, never the FACT.

how_to_answer: Rewrite the WORDS so this story clears every rule above and answers every reason in `held_for`. Same number of segments, same order. Use ONLY numbers you can derive from each segment's `data.points` (or a year that appears as a label). If `judge` is present, its `problems`/`fixes` are what the video editor saw on the RENDERED video — shorter topics and one clear number per line are what fix 'unreadable' and 'text on text'. Write answer_path as one JSON object matching answer_schema, request_id and slug copied, and commit it. Do not touch the request.
